newsitem.title: USA: Zitel says transition affecting royalties.
newsitem.headline: Zitel says transition affecting royalties.

text.p: Zitel Corp, a maker of high-performance computer storage systems, on Tuesday said a product transition from an early generation product, called RAMAC 2, to the new RAMAC 3 affected fiscal second quarter royalty payments to the company.

"While it is still early in the transition, it is difficult to gauge how the increased capacity of RAMAC 3 will impact our royalties" going forward, Chief Executive Officer Jack King said in a statement.
Earlier, the company reported net loss of $0.13 a share on sales of $2.8 million for the second quarter ended March 31.

The second quarter fiscal 1997 net loss compared to a profit of $0.06 per share on sales of $5.5 million last year. The 1997 results reflected a tax benefit of $1.0 million versus a tax provision of $659,000 one year ago.
Zitel said the decline in royalties during the quarter came in royalties from International Business Machines Corp.

King said sales of the company's CASD product were hurt by restructuring the sales and marketing operations. Also the company enhanced its product line by adding a 9-gigabyte computer drive and a solid state disk features in its CASD-II/Enterprise storage system.

"With the majority of the changes to our sales and marketing infrastructure in place, and the significant increase in business opportunities we have generated, we are poised for improvement in our CASD product sales," King said.
